gloss: to hold up to the light; to leave a gap

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {透|す}かしていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to hold up to the light; to look through
definitions.explanation: To hold something up against a light source in order to see through it, often to check for watermarks, flaws, or hidden features.

definitions.gloss: to leave a gap; to thin out
definitions.explanation: To create space between things, such as thinning out branches or leaving gaps for ventilation.

examples.japanese: {紙|かみ}を{光|ひかり}に{透|す}かして{見|み}た。
examples.english: I held the paper up to the light to look at it.

examples.japanese: お{札|さつ}を{透|す}かすと、{透|す}かし{模様|もよう}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: If you hold a banknote up to the light, you can see the watermark.

examples.japanese: {木漏|こも}れ{日|び}が{葉|は}を{透|す}かして{差|さ}し{込|こ}んでいた。
examples.english: Sunlight was filtering through the leaves.

examples.japanese: {枝|えだ}を{透|す}かして{風通|かぜとお}しをよくする。
examples.english: Thin out the branches to improve air circulation.

examples.japanese: {前髪|まえがみ}を{透|す}かして{軽|かる}くしてもらった。
examples.english: I had my bangs thinned out to make them lighter.

examples.japanese: {植木|うえき}の{葉|は}を{透|す}かしてやらないと、{虫|むし}がつきやすくなる。
examples.english: If you don't thin out the garden plant's leaves, it becomes more susceptible to insects.

notes:
Godan verb (す・か・す). The transitive counterpart of {透|す}ける (to be transparent, to show through).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {光|ひかり}に{透|す}かす (to hold up to the light)
- {透|す}かして{見|み}る (to look at something by holding it up to light)
- {透|す}かし{模様|もよう} (watermark pattern)
- {枝|えだ}を{透|す}かす (to thin out branches)
- {髪|かみ}を{透|す}かす (to thin out hair)

Sense 1 is the more commonly encountered meaning. The connection between the two senses is the idea of allowing light or air to pass through by creating openings.
